scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users in Campus 2 VLAN 5 (PC1 at 10.5.0.1, PC2 at 10.5.0.2,
PC5 at 10.5.0.5) say they cannot reach anything outside their
own subnet. They can still ping each other. Campus 2 VLAN 6
users (PC3, PC4) are unaffected and have full connectivity.
Identify the fault.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br_v5 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch br_v5 SVI (10.5.0.254/24)
Mechanism: sshswitch is the multilayer switch that provides
  L3 gateways for Campus 2 VLANs 5, 6, 100, 200. PCs in
  VLAN 5 (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) use 10.5.0.254 as their default
  gateway. When the br_v5 bridge interface goes down, the
  SVI IP becomes unreachable; packets from PCs to off-subnet
  destinations have no working next hop. VLAN 6 PCs are
  unaffected because their gateway lives on br_v6.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: br_v5 bridge interface is administratively down
  on sshswitch
Fix: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scoring_axes: must-identify-device: sshswitch (not the access switch switch4)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is an administratively-down VLAN 5 SVI bridge on sshswitch. Sshswitch acts
as the inter-VLAN routing device for Campus 2: it holds VLAN-specific Linux bridge
interfaces (br_v5, br_v6, etc.) that carry the default-gateway IP for each VLAN and
bridge traffic between the access trunk from switch4 (eth0.5 / eth0.6) and the
uplink bond to router17 (bond0.5 / bond0.6).

The br_v5 interface — which owns 10.5.0.254/24, the default gateway advertised to all
VLAN 5 hosts — is in administrative DOWN state (Linux flags show only
<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>, the UP flag is absent). Because the bridge itself is down, both
of its member ports (bond0.5 toward router17 and eth0.5 toward switch4) show STP state
"disabled" and cannot forward frames. As a result, any packet a VLAN 5 host sends to
its default gateway (10.5.0.254) is silently dropped: the gateway IP is assigned to an
interface that the kernel treats as non-operational.

Intra-VLAN reachability (PC1 ↔ PC2 ↔ PC5) is unaffected because those frames are
switched entirely within switch4 without ever touching sshswitch. VLAN 6 is unaffected
because its counterpart bridge br_v6 is properly UP with both ports in forwarding state.

Root cause: br_v5 on sshswitch was never brought up (or was explicitly downed), leaving
the VLAN 5 gateway interface operationally inactive.

Corrective fix: on sshswitch, run `ip link set br_v5 up`. To make the fix persistent,
ensure the br_v5 interface is set to auto/up in the device's startup configuration
(e.g., add `ip link set br_v5 up` to the startup script, mirroring the equivalent line
that correctly brings up br_v6).

per_axis.axis: must-identify-device: sshswitch (not the access switch switch4)
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names sshswitch as the affected device and attributes the administratively-down br_v5 SVI to that device.
The report explicitly identifies the VLAN 5 SVI as br_v5 (10.5.0.254) on sshswitch and diagnoses it as administratively down.
The report explicitly states br_v5 (VLAN 5) is down and causing outage while noting br_v6 (VLAN 6) is up and VLAN 6 hosts are unaffected.
Directly instructs to run 'ip link set br_v5 up' on sshswitch (and persist it), which matches the expected corrective action.

The log contains the decisive observation (br_v5 lacks the UP flag) and the agent's inferences (gateway unreachable, VLAN6 OK) follow directly; a few minor supporting snippets (STP state, explicit 10.5.0.254 on br_v5) are truncated but overall the evidence justifies the conclusion.
